page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-32 is a general-purpose compute instance configured to provide balanced resource density for enterprise-scale workloads. The machine is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 32 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem incorporates a 55 MB Level 3 cache, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache and 0.25 MB L2 cache per core. Memory capacity is fixed at 128 GB, maintaining a 4 GB per virtual core ratio characteristic of standard profile instances. The platform does not incorporate dedicated GPU accelerators or local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence must be attached through network-based block storage.

Instruction set support includes standard vector extensions such as AVX alongside BMI2 and FMA, paired with hardware-accelerated AES encryption. However, modern vector and matrix extensions like AVX-512, AMX, and SHA-NI are absent. In synthetic and realistic performance benchmarks, the e2-standard-32 exhibits mid-tier multi-threaded results. The system recorded a PassMark CPU score of 38,099.23, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,295, and sustained stress-ng multi-core throughput of 42,996.45. Memory bandwidth reaches 98.83 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 44.29 GB/sec on large-block writes. Conversely, single-threaded performance is more constrained, registering lower-tier results in gzip compression and single-core Geekbench tasks.

Operational throughput benchmarks confirm stable behavior across concurrent service workloads. The instance achieves 21.98 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 18.06 GB/sec in static web serving tests, while handling PassMark database operations at 12,626.08. CPU-based machine learning inference achieves 50.08 prompt processing tokens per second on 7-billion-parameter models. From an efficiency perspective, the instance provides cost-effective vertical scalability for thread-dense execution without paying the premium of compute-specialized or high-frequency instances. The primary tradeoff lies in moderate single-thread execution speeds and reliance on networked storage for disk I/O. The e2-standard-32 is well positioned for containerized microservice backends, multi-threaded CI/CD builders, medium-scale relational databases, and high-concurrency web applications.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute and memory scaling. Built on the x86_64 architecture using 2.2 GHz Intel Xeon processors, it provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 128 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. The instance features a 55 MB L3 cache, basic AVX acceleration, and hardware AES encryption, though it omits AVX-512 extensions, dedicated GPUs, and onboard local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the instance consistently demonstrates middle-tier performance across multi-threaded operations, including Geekbench multi-core processing, static web serving throughput at 18.06 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations exceeding 21 million operations per second. However, single-threaded throughput ranks lower in compression benchmarks. Positioned as a cost-efficient resource tier, the e2-standard-32 is best matched for enterprise application hosting, microservices fleets, relational databases relying on remote block storage, and mid-range continuous integration pipelines.
og_description: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 32 vCPUs, 128 GB of RAM, and reliable middle-tier throughput for enterprise web serving, microservices, and databases without local storage.

tagline: A 32-vCPU general-purpose compute instance delivering balanced memory allocation, consistent multi-threaded execution, and cost-efficient scaling for business-critical enterprise workloads.
bullet_points: 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon processors at 2.2 GHz
128 GB system memory maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio
